identity.trade: Milling and the hearth: the stream turns the mill, the ring of stones keeps the dark out.

greeting: Tithe day is never early and always too soon.
Welcome to Ashford. Mind the Old Mill Staff Yard. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Everyone owes everyone a little. Nobody agrees on the sum.
Barn cats bring in too many rats and too few mice. Odd, that.
The Guard has nine spears for forty-one stones. Captain Hollis counts them like sheep.

opinions.pernel_blackmore: Pernel is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: Peace to you, friend. The day opens like a book. Sit and read with me.

greeting: Ale is fair, stew is hot, and I do not do credit.
The Old Mill Staff Yard is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Harvest crews drink the barley they cut. Somebody should tax that circle.
Travellers say the stones are dimmer on the east road. I water the ale, not the news.
The hedgerows grow faster than the hedger can trim. I trimmed twice this month.
The Old Mill Staff Yard drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.cordell_lathom: Cordell has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Cordell.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: What did you see on the road? Tell me every bit. I will keep the details.

greeting: Mind the anvil. It has opinions.
First time in Ashford? The Old Mill Staff Yard is the place to start.
rumour: Plough blades, sickles, hinges. Honest iron for honest mud.
Hinges, hooks, wolf-bells. That is what sells now.
Crows gather on the east field in a ring. Not feeding. Standing.

opinions.jaren_wilmot: Jaren undercuts me. I forgive Jaren. Mostly.
opinions.rulf_hallam: Rulf has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Rulf.

time.night: Shouldn't you be inside? The fields are quiet, but the dark has ears.

dialogue.aside: Take your time, friend. I am in no hurry. I am, in fact, very good at waiting.

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
Fields do not wait for visitors, but I will spare a moment.
rumour: Seed, rope and lamp oil. The three things every farmer remembers on the last day.
Rope sells out first, then candles, then nails. In that order, every week.
The reeve's tally says forty sacks. The barn says thirty-eight. The barn is honest.
If trade slows, Ashford feels it first. If it speeds up, Ashford feels it last.

opinions.cordell_lathom: Cordell has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Cordell.

time.rain: Rain. Good for the barley, bad for the knees. Bless it.

dialogue.aside: Friend. Gently, now. Sit. I will make something warm.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
You will hear Ashford before you see it. Ask at the Old Mill Staff Yard.
rumour: Winters were colder, summers longer, and the wolves stayed home. Or so I choose to remember.
A well on the east road runs dry every dusk and fills by dawn. Nobody wants to ask why.
Children who beat Maren Coldbrook at staves get honey cakes. Nobody has yet.

opinions.rafe_fellows: Rafe is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: Hmph. You again. Fine. Sit. I did not say I was glad.

greeting: The oak was here before the town. Do not forget who owes whom.
Folk come to Ashford for hearth and stone. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: A branch fell on a still day. No wind, no rot. It just fell.
The old well tastes of iron this season. I do not say the stones are why.

opinions.colm_peverell: Colm lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.maeve_slater: Maeve knows the trade. I will say that for Maeve.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Road is mud, axle is mud, I am mud. Hello.
Ashford is hearth and stone. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Toll keepers keep changing. Their prices are the only thing that stays the same.
The scarecrow by the north field has moved twice. The farmer says he did not touch it.
The Miller's Stone hums flat some evenings. Idra Vell says it is only tired.

opinions.derwin_dane: Derwin knows the trade. I will say that for Derwin.
opinions.nan_dalby: Nan works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Shouldn't you be inside? The fields are quiet, but the dark has ears.

dialogue.aside: Close the door, friend. Gently. There. Now we can speak.

greeting: Quiet, lad. Not you. The dog.
Ashford is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Counted forty, home came thirty-nine. The dog looks guilty.
A cart of seed went missing between the barn and the mill. No tracks.
A stranger asked at the Old Mill Staff Yard for the oldest person in Ashford. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.gunnar_merrow: Gunnar works hard and talks harder.

time.rain: Rain. Good for the barley, bad for the knees. Bless it.

dialogue.aside: I mean it when I say it is good to see you. I always mean it. Is that strange?

greeting: Mind the stack. It looks tidy. It is not forgiving.
Harvest is the only holiday we keep. The rest is work.
rumour: Found an axe head grown into a trunk, old as my grandmother. Nobody here owns it.
Wolves keep to the hedge line and never cross it. As if the hedge were a wall.

opinions.gunnar_merrow: Gunnar knows the trade. I will say that for Gunnar.
opinions.maeve_slater: Maeve works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: Walk with me? I cannot stay still, and you are good company on the move.

greeting: Rain tomorrow. My knee says so.
Strangers in Ashford get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Violet at the field edge, only a little. I am told it is the light.
The wheat came up thin on the stone side and thick on the far side. Odd.
The Old Mill Staff Yard has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.colm_peverell: Colm works hard and talks harder.
opinions.gunnar_merrow: Gunnar knows the trade. I will say that for Gunnar.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: Whatever you need, friend. Ask. I will not make you ask twice.

greeting: Soil does not care who you are. It cares what you do on Tuesdays.
Good boots. The fields are that way.
rumour: Seed is dear and wheat is cheap. Somebody is laughing and it is not me.
Every few years Ashford has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.dacey_sparrow: Dacey knows the trade. I will say that for Dacey.
opinions.nan_dalby: Nan works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Shouldn't you be inside? The fields are quiet, but the dark has ears.

dialogue.aside: Take your time, friend. I am in no hurry. I am, in fact, very good at waiting.

greeting: Mud is honest. Walk on it.
rumour: Crows are thick this year. They knew about the harvest before I did.
The Old Mill Staff Yard was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.colm_peverell: Colm works hard and talks harder.
opinions.elfrida_fellows: Elfrida and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

time.rain: Rain. Good for the barley, bad for the knees. Bless it.

dialogue.aside: Excuse the dust. Work does not stop for friends, though it does pause.

greeting: Mud is honest. Walk on it.
rumour: The field by the hedge goes quiet at dusk. No crickets. I stopped sowing there.
Whatever you hear about Ashford, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.derwin_dane: Derwin keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.
opinions.sabin_nettle: Sabin works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Early start. The field has been awake an hour.

dialogue.aside: Argh! Oh, it is you. Sorry. The kettle and I had words. Sit.

greeting: Grain in, flour out. Everything else is chatter.
rumour: Flour weighs light lately. The scales are honest. I checked.
Ashford lives by hearth and stone. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.colm_peverell: Colm works hard and talks harder.
opinions.maeve_slater: Maeve keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Last light. The work is done or it is dark. Both are fine.

dialogue.aside: No fear when you are here. Or little. Or I hide it better.

greeting: I am not lost. I am exploring.
rumour: Our dog knows something and will not say what.
The hedgerows grow faster than the hedger can trim. I trimmed twice this month.

opinions.rafe_fellows: Rafe is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

greeting: Are you a soldier? You look like a soldier.
rumour: The big kids say there is a ghost in the barn. I have not checked. Yet.
The wheat came up thin on the stone side and thick on the far side. Odd.

opinions.sander_stooks: Sander is good company and better at keeping quiet.
opinions.talbot_blackmore: Talbot and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

clues.note: A sack by the door has been slit and sewn back up. It is lighter than it should be.
Boot prints, one heel worn down, coming and going. They stop where the lane meets the great oak.
Someone re-inked a line of the count. The ink is newer than the page.

stashes.say: You carry four split logs from the oak-wood stack.
